title: Introduce Invocation Microtelescope and Cost Signal Router for fine-grained observability
author: Anika Rao
description: Motivation: production SREs and platform engineers frequently need highly targeted per-invocation signals (token-level cost, phase latency, kv-cache warm/ miss markers) without ingesting full traces for every request. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) Invocation Microtelescope: a lightweight per-invocation micro-telemetry packet that captures a compact token-phase breakdown, kernel warmup hint, and a small set of trace anchors. Microtelescope is designed to be emitted at configurable sampling rates and can be routed independently of full traces. 2) Cost Signal Router: a pipeline-level router that classifies cost-related telemetry (microtelescope, token-cost rollups, and coarse traces) and directs them to different retention/alerting destinations (short-retention hot-index, long-retention cost-store, SLO-alerting queue) based on configurable policies (tenant tier, route, cost-per-invocation thresholds). What changed: - New binary protobuf for microtelescope packet and serializer with a shipper shim (redwood/telemetry/microtelescope.go, redwood/telemetry/microtelescope.proto). - Router and policy implementation (redwood/observability/cost_router.py) with unit tests and fixtures. - SDK change: Python client now emits an optional microtelescope hint header to reduce parsing work on server side (redwood-sdk-python/redwood/transport.py). - Dashboard: Grafana panels for microtelescope-derived token-phase sparklines and per-route cost-router metrics (redwood-observability/dashboards/cost-router.json). - Alerts: tuned SLO alert rule that uses routed signals to reduce noisy alerts for low-value tenants (infra/alerts/slo-cost-routing.yaml). Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag (telemetry.microtelescope.enabled) and default-sampled at 0.1% for hosted tier; can be increased for Dedicated customers. Backwards compatibility: router accepts older packets and falls back to legacy routing path. Performance/backpressure: microtelescope serializer is ~400 bytes compressed and the router has flow-control hooks to drop low-priority packets under memory pressure. Testing: local unit tests, integration tests with mini-router, and a staged rollout to beta tenants. Related: ENG-1987 tracks signal retention product work; SUP-4123 triggered a hotfix request during an incident that motivated lower-noise routing. Checklist: - [x] Proto and serializers implemented - [x] Router policies + unit tests - [x] SDK hint header update - [x] Grafana panels and alert tuning - [x] Add e2e integration test harness - [x] Document rollout gates and RBAC controls

review_comments: Samir Patel (2026-02-11): Can we quantify memory and CPU overhead at 1% sample? Please add microbenchmarks for serializer and router hot path.

Anika Rao (2026-02-12): Added a microbench in tests/bench/test_microtelescope_bench.go and included numbers in the PR description. At 1% sample on a c5.4xlarge-equivalent, CPU overhead < 0.6% and mean serialization latency is 80µs.

Jordan Liu (2026-02-13): Router policy looks good. Request: make default policy explicitly deny routing to long-retention index for dev tenants. Also add a feature flag to disable token-level enrichment for regulated tenants.
Anika Rao (2026-02-14): Added tenant checks and a config toggle telemetry.router.allow_long_retention in policies.py and documented smoke tests.
release_notes: Introduces Invocation Microtelescope (compact per-invocation telemetry) and a Cost Signal Router to separate high-volume token-level signals from long-retention cost stores. Feature gated and off by default; see rollout docs for increasing sampling for Dedicated customers.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature gate telemetry.microtelescope.enabled in stage for 72h before enabling on prod.
Monitor router.queue_drop_rate and microtelescope.payload_size for first 48h.
If under memory pressure, reduce microtelescope sampling to 0.01% via runtime flag.
